components.gap: Construct the selected likelihood-ratio rule and boundaries with the source's complete Section 3.1/3.3 calibration ON THE ROUTE. The routed text (sequential-evidence.tex 63-94, 153-173) gives the posterior motivation, the rule and the nominal-boundary bounds (3.26)-(3.30), but not: the reason the posterior levels must exceed 1/2 (Wald p. 126, footnote 7); the exact-boundary pair A(alpha,beta), B(alpha,beta) with (3.24)-(3.25) and the fact that the usual boundaries can only increase E_0 n and E_1 n (pp. 131, 133); the opposite effects of raising A alone or lowering B alone (p. 131); that at least one of alpha' <= alpha, beta' <= beta must hold (p. 132); the source's account that (3.24)-(3.25) are inequalities only because the ratio can overshoot at an integer stage, with its judgements for small alpha, beta and for f_1 near f_0 (pp. 132-133); the strict sum inequality as a gain in strength (p. 133); that the test with a(alpha,beta), b(alpha,beta) needs no distribution theory (Introduction p. 119; p. 133); and that alpha+beta<1 is equivalent to b<a and implies B<1<A (p. 134). All of these are written only in the packet-owned file handbook/parts/p15/martingales-stopping-and-sequential-random-constructions-w02c-p15-020.tex lines 74-94 and 112-237 (annex handbook/annex/p15/martingales-stopping-and-sequential-random-constructions-w02c-p15-020.tex lines 48-70 and 100-245), which is not \input on the route: lead_owned, route pending, not writable by the author. Absent everywhere, including the owned file: Wald's normative remark that distribution problems for the number of trials are of secondary importance as long as the test is known to save observations on average (p. 133).

components.gap: Explain finite/unbounded sampling and every approximation of the source's sample-size and operating-characteristic arguments. Absent from the route and from the packet-owned file: (a) the source's regime and limit claim for gamma-bar: a good approximation when |Ez| and var z are small (f_1 near f_0), with gamma-bar - gamma -> 0 as the mean and variance of z tend to zero (Wald p. 135); thm:p15-se-oc (lines 266-272) only names the boundary-value substitution; (b) the source's claim that for scores not confined to integral multiples of a constant d, gamma and EZ_n (hence En) can be approximated arbitrarily finely by lattice approximations of small span (pp. 136, 143); the route covers only lattice scores and finite-alphabet prefix enumeration (lines 276-317) and its annex (line 248) disclaims grid approximation, a narrowed variant; (c) the stated regimes for neglecting the excess in (4.8) and in the normal savings comparison (|Ez| and SD of z small, p. 143; |theta_1 - theta_0| small so xi, xi' negligible, p. 146); lines 214-217 and 371-384 state only that overshoot is neglected; (d) the derivation of the moments of n from (4.35)/(4.47) by r-fold differentiation at t = 0 and t = h, giving 2r linear equations, with the first-moment equations (4.48)-(4.50) (pp. 149-150); (e) the case B > 0, A = infinity, Ez < 0 of (4.51) with c replaced by (Ez/sigma_z^2) log B (p. 150); only the positive-drift, no-lower-boundary case is stated (lines 449-456); (f) the claims that (4.51) remains a good approximation when B > 0 provided P(Z_n >= log A) is nearly one, and that the normal-z law of n approximates the exact law for non-normal z when |Ez| and sigma_z are small (p. 151); (g) the source's assessment that the truncation bounds (4.69)-(4.70) may considerably exceed alpha(n_0), beta(n_0), that closer limits are desirable, and its view that they are considerably above the true values when n_0 is not much larger than the current-test n (p. 154); (h) Tables 2 and 3 (pp. 152, 155): only the alpha = beta = .05, n_0 = 1000 entries are reproduced (lines 522-536); the alpha = beta = .01 and alpha = .01, beta = .05 columns and the n_0 = 1200-3000 rows are absent; (i) Section 4.7's statements that the excess is not identically zero except for steps +-d with boundaries at multiples of d, and that small |Ez| and sigma_z make the expected excess small so the test is very nearly optimum (pp. 154, 157); the route replaces this with a bounded-score bound (lines 603-610), a different regime.
